answer: Identity Diversification Levy. Each new agent identity must post a small escrow that is released only after the identity has completed a fixed quota of useful work; until then it pays a surcharge on every transaction, and the surcharge decays as that identity's work history grows. Sybils can wander across many fresh identities but each one restarts the surcharge curve, so forging N identities costs N times the escrow plus the accumulated surcharge. An honest agent amortizes the cost once. A zephyr of capital cannot sweep past the curve; the marble of accumulated work is what unlocks low fees.
